maria: Pushed an NSYS + perfetto capture from the long-seq repro (seqlen=4096) — grabbed while the prod replica hit the bandwidth spike. link: https://perfetto.app/trace/ABCDEF (nsys: out.nsys)
maria: TL;DR: repeated short-lived KV lookup kernels correlated with ~600-750 GB/s HBM bursts, followed by a couple of large attention kernels. Looks like read amplification from KV path causing contention.
akshay: Can you paste the kernel timeline snippet and the top kernels by aggregate time? small bullets are fine.
maria: Timeline excerpt (nsys flame):
```
- kv_lookup_kernel (many small launches, 200-500us each)
- kv_prefetch_kernel (short spikes, high DRAM reads)
- attention_fwd_cuda (longer, but not the main spike source)
- cudaMemcpyAsync (DMA bursts coincident with kv_lookup)
```
Top kernels by total time: `attention_fwd_cuda`, `kv_lookup_kernel`, `kv_reconcile`, `softmax_cuda`.
perf-bot: Regression detector: PR #8423 increased KV miss rate on long-seq path by 2.3x — flagged at 2026-03-15T14:06Z :warning:
lee: That PR changed microbatch coalescing heuristics, right? We removed prefix coalescing to reduce tail latency for small requests.
olivia: I ran a local instrumented build and reproduced. NVPROF shows repeated small device reads and a high number of PCIe DMA submissions. nvprof top events:
```
GPU memory read throughput: spikes to ~700 GB/s (sustained ~150ms bursts)
Kernel launch overhead dominating when launches are many and tiny
PCIe submit stalls visible in driver traces
```
sam: Hypothesis: new batching heuristic picks `generic_kv_v3` when it should pick the small-window specialized kernel. v3 has a higher per-launch memory footprint and causes more page-crossing reads -> read amplification.
maria: Evidence: in perfetto slices the DMA timeline lines up with kv_lookup_kernel launches and there are repeated cacheline-sized reads rather than coalesced range reads. Also observed HBM read stall counters rising sharply during these windows.
akshay: Quick experiments to run:
- run nsys with `--trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt` and collect per-kernel `dram_read_transactions` counters
- repro with `KV_WINDOW=on` vs `off` to test coalescer
- A/B the previous microbatching heuristic (pre-PR vs post-PR)
olivia: I already ran `KV_WINDOW=on` locally: coalescer reduced number of launches by ~40% and peak BW by ~35% in the local trace. But there was a small tail latency regress for tiny requests.
maria: Suggest we try an adaptive policy: enable coalescer for seqlen >= 2048 or when predicted active KV windows > 64. Also try forcing `kv_kernel_v2_small` selection for windowed reads in the scheduler and re-run nsys.
infra-bot: Repro job scheduled on `dedicated-gpu-12` -> job-6721, ETA start 2026-03-16T14:30Z. Artifacts will land to gs://redwood-perf/job-6721/
akshay: If the coalescer fix works, we should add a microbenchmark that randomizes seq len and asserts peak BW doesn't exceed baseline by >10%.
sam: Also add kernel-selection unit tests and a perf regression check that runs the long-seq profile nightly for a week (to catch flakey alignment issues).
maria: I'll attach the raw nsys `out.nsys` and a small script to reproduce the sequence distribution. Putting both in the job artifacts. Thanks everyone, will post updates after the dedicated run.
lee: SGTM. if infra can also capture `nvlink` counters (if present) that might show cross-GPU pressure.
maria: noted, added to job config. :thumbsup:
